raw_response:
*Speaking as the farmer:*

Aiya, another year. My back still hurts from last autumn but what can you do, the land doesn't wait. Let me think through this season.

I got 13 mu and some. For the wheat-maize, I'll do maybe 8 mu — same fields I always do, out past the road. The other 5 mu I'll keep in cotton like before. My husband's brother said switch it all to maize because cotton price is bad, but cotton I know. Forty years I've grown cotton. And my daughter-in-law helps with the picking, she's good at it. Switching to something new at my age, no.

Wheat first. I put it in around early October after I clear the maize stubble. My nephew comes with his tractor, he charges me but less than outside people. I use the same seed the seed shop sells, whatever everyone in the village is buying — I don't remember the name, it's in a red bag. Before sowing I spread about 2 bags of compound fertilizer across every mu, that's the one with three numbers on it. Then in spring when the wheat starts standing up, I throw urea on top, maybe half a bag per mu, depends how yellow it looks. If it looks green and strong I use less, save the money.

I water the wheat maybe three times — once after sowing if the ground is dry, once in spring when it's jointing, once when the grain is filling. The well is shared with my cousin's family, we take turns. Pumping costs money, the electric meter runs fast. I try not to water more than needed.

Last year I got about 450 kg per mu of wheat, the year before was worse because of that late frost. This year I'll hope for similar, maybe 450.

Then maize right after wheat harvest in June. No time to rest, you cut the wheat in the morning and by afternoon the neighbor is already planting maize. I use the no-till planter, my nephew runs it through. Seeds I buy fresh, hybrid kind, can't save maize seed. Fertilizer I put down with the planter, one bag per mu of compound, then another urea topdress when it's about knee-high. Maize doesn't need as much water if the summer rain comes. Maybe I irrigate once or twice only.

Maize yield usually 500 kg per mu if the weather is okay. Last year was dry in August so I only got 420.

Cotton is the hardest. I start turning the soil in April, plant late April. Cotton seed I buy from the supply shop. I put compound fertilizer before planting and urea when the buds come. Cotton needs spraying — bollworms, aphids, all of it. I spray three or four times through the summer, my son helps with the sprayer on weekends when he's back from the city. Picking takes the whole family — me, my daughter-in-law, sometimes my sister comes. We pick three times from September to October.

Cotton yield maybe 250 kg of lint per mu, not great but steady.

Money is tight. Nine mouths to feed, and my grandson needs school things. I can't afford to put extra fertilizer "just in case" like the big farmers. I use what I've always used. If it works, it works.
